Several nodes are now closed:
- **Supported:** H1.1 and H1.1.1 (the base recipe clears the bar at 9–10 epochs). H1.1.2 is supported after being rewritten as "the knee is in (8.5, 9] epochs"; its original "at least 1 extra epoch needed" clause is refuted.
- **Refuted:** H1.1.3 (the slope is not linear and is below 0.4 pp per epoch), H1.3 and H1.3.1 (label smoothing 0.2 and 0.3 give the same result), H2.2 and H2.2.1 (the train step is GPU-bound, not launch-bound; I took E010 off H2.2 because it was misattributed there), and H3 (fixed overhead is about 2%, not over 10%). H3.1 and H3.2 stay supported as maintenance items.
- **Retired:** H2.1 and H2.1.1, because compile, channels_last and bf16 have been in the base since E001 and E007 tested something else.
- **Supported:** H4.2 and H4.2.1 (lookahead is worth about 1 pp; I dropped the clause claiming it reduces spread).

H4.1 now holds an explicit noise model and is marked inconclusive. Bit-identical reruns are deterministic, but any code change re-draws the 3-seed mean with an sd of about 0.09 pp, and time jitter is about 1%.

Several nodes were restated:
- **H1:** the new target is a knee below 8 epochs, at 7.3 s or less.
- **H2:** headroom is now about 5–10% from cutting work, with lower confidence.
- **H4:** the binding constraint is the local 0.753 gate, with winner's-curse risk.
- **H1.2.1:** Muon with lookahead kept and batch size 1024, compared at 9 epochs.
- **H1.4.1:** a self-scoring version with no separate proxy model, at low priority.
- **H1.5.1:** widening beyond the current 576 channels.

New nodes:
- **N1 (end-of-training noise, the top lever):** averaging and lr-tail changes, plus a combined 8.5-epoch target.
- **N2:** an lr/wd/momentum sweep.
- **N3:** an 8.75-epoch test of the knee.
- **N4 (non-conv kernels):** E010 is its first evidence, and N4a tests SiLU or ReLU in place of GELU.
- **N5 (conv-shape inefficiency):** a cold-cache paired rerun that checks whether the E007 keep was noise, and a test of the whitening output shape.
- **N6:** whether Muon needs lookahead.
- **N7:** checking the tip on extra seeds.
- **N8:** mild brightness/contrast augmentation.

Suggested priority: N1a/N1b, then N3, then H1.2.1 and N6, then N4a, then N2a, then H1.5.1."}

updates.reason: E005- (H2.2.1): fused/foreach plus a fully compiled step saved ~0% time. The E003 profile shows GPU time ~= wall time and the SGD step at ~2.3% of the step. E010 was misattributed here: replacing the pool backward is a non-conv kernel change, not launch or optimizer overhead, and it moves to a new node. The SiLU item was also moved to the new non-conv-kernel node.
E005-: time -0.03% against a >=8% prediction. The premise (launch-bound) is contradicted by the E003 profile.

The only support is generic (MosaicML's recipe for ResNet-56). E006 suggests the accuracy-vs-epoch curve is steep near the knee, so lower-resolution early epochs risk costing more than they save. Deprioritized.
Untested. Prior lowered for the same reasons as H2.3.

E001: prepare takes 0.06-0.15 s. The E003 profile puts per-epoch overheads (augment, randperm/gather, lookahead) at ~0.16 s per run, ~2% of total. The fixed-overhead share is ~2-3%, not >10%. The H3.1/H3.2 mechanisms are already implemented, which is why overhead is small.
Implemented since E001: the train set sits on the GPU as uint8 with GPU augmentation. Prepare takes <=0.15 s and the step is GPU-bound (E003 profile). Now a maintenance item.
E001 prepare took 0.06-0.15 s (<=1.0 s). In the E003 profile GPU time ~= wall time, so the run is not CPU-bound.

Implemented since E001 and maintained through E007/E010: all shapes are compiled and warmed in build(). Now a maintenance item. Caveat: the Inductor autotune cache state differs between builds (E008), and the official judge builds from a cold cache.
E003 profile: step time is flat at 18.8 ms over 8x48 steps, and 432 x 18.8 ms ~= 8.12 s of the 8.3 s train time, so there are no recompiles in the timed region. Eval passes on every complete run.

updates.statement: The binding constraint is the local 0.753 gate on fixed seeds 0-2, not the official 40-seed 0.75 bar. Any code change re-draws the 3-seed mean (sd ~0.09 pp), so keep decisions near the gate risk a winner's curse. Measuring the noise and reducing variance through averaging lets a recipe run closer to its knee without being fragile.
updates.reason: Restated per the review. The tip's 3-seed mean of 0.7551 implies an expected 40-seed mean of ~0.755 +- 0.13, well clear of 0.75. The gate is what binds, and five near-identical recipes span 0.7542-0.7560.

updates.statement: A bit-identical commit reruns deterministically in accuracy, with ~1% timing jitter. But any code change, including math-identical compile-graph changes, re-draws each seed's outcome: the 3-seed-mean sd is ~0.09 pp and the per-seed sd is ~0.2 pp. Accuracy deltas under ~0.25 pp and single-run time deltas under ~1.5% are therefore inconclusive by rule.
updates.reason: Partially refuted. E003 shows bit-identical accuracy and +0.9% time, supporting the narrow claim. E005 (identical math, different graph) moved accuracy by -0.18 pp, and E008 drifted +0.9% in time in the opposite direction from the one predicted, so neither noise source is 'small' next to the 1-2% systems effects and ~0.1-0.2 pp recipe effects under test. Restated as an explicit noise model.

updates.statement: Rerunning an identical (bit-identical commit) recipe gives a spread in mean accuracy of <=0.15 pp and a spread in mean time of <=3%.
updates.reason: E003+: accuracy identical to E002 to every digit, time +0.9%. Re-scoped to bit-identical commits, since it does not cover the re-draw that code changes cause.

updates.statement: Weight averaging (lookahead or EMA) raises accuracy strongly at low epoch counts on CIFAR-100: about 1 pp at 9 epochs, worth ~1-2 epochs. That is much more than on CIFAR-10 (about 11% of epochs).
updates.reason: E008+: removing lookahead cost 0.99 pp, and all three seeds dropped by 0.7-1.2 pp, far beyond re-draw noise. The 'lowers spread' clause was dropped as unsupported: the per-seed range is 0.51 pp without lookahead vs 0.47 pp with it.

updates.statement: Removing lookahead from the airbench96-style base costs >=0.3 pp of mean accuracy at a fixed epoch count (about 1 epoch).
updates.reason: E008+: -0.99 pp at 9 epochs, about 3x the predicted size, consistent across seeds. The std clause was not supported (no variance increase visible) and is removed.

new.statement: At <=9 epochs on CIFAR-100, noise in the final iterate (lr 9 with LS and 100 classes) limits accuracy. Averaging and annealing the end of training are therefore the strongest recipe levers. The lookahead schedule (0.95^5*(t/T)^3, every 5 steps), the lr decay tail and momentum 0.85 were all inherited untuned from CIFAR-10.

At 9 epochs on the tip, a stronger or denser averaging setup gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time. Candidates: a higher base lookahead decay, lookahead every 3 steps instead of 5, or an EMA over the last ~30% of steps applied on top of lookahead.
At 9 epochs, a sharper lr anneal over the final ~15% of steps gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy with time unchanged. Candidates: a faster decay to zero in the last epoch, or a lower terminal lr.
Combining the best averaging and tail changes (N1a/N1b) lets the recipe clear 0.753 at 8.5 epochs, with time <=7.75 s on top of the E010 systems changes.
lr 9, wd 0.012 and momentum 0.85 come from CIFAR-10 airbench and are mistuned for CIFAR-100 at 9 epochs. A small sweep recovers accuracy that is worth part of an epoch.
In a one-factor sweep at 9 epochs (lr in {6, 12}, wd in {0.008, 0.016}), at least one setting beats the tip's mean accuracy by >=0.25 pp, which is above re-draw noise.
The tip recipe (E010) at 8.75 epochs, with the schedule scaled to the step count, reaches mean accuracy >=0.753 in <=7.9 s. Expected accuracy is 0.751-0.755.

Non-conv kernels that take a visible share of GPU time can be cut with no or neutral change to accuracy, mainly by doing less work. Examples are the atomic/scatter backward of adaptive pooling and the memory-bound fused BN/GELU elementwise kernels (~3.4 ms/step, ~18%). E010 is the first instance: max_pool2d replaced adaptive_max_pool2d, -2.0% time.

Replacing GELU with SiLU (or ReLU) throughout cuts mean time by >=3% versus the tip, with mean accuracy within +-0.15 pp (re-draw noise). Before launching, run a one-step finite-gradient check under compile.

The cuDNN convs run at ~30% of bf16 peak (~95 TFLOP/s) because of layer shapes, not because the wrong algorithm is selected. Likely causes are the 31x31 output of the unpadded 2x2 whitening conv and the small late-block spatial sizes. Autotuning or algorithm selection (max-autotune, cudnn.benchmark) recovers <=~1%, and that gain may not transfer to the PCIe judge.

After clearing the Inductor cache, run the E010 commit and an E010 variant without cudnn.benchmark and max-autotune 2-3 times each, interleaved. The paired mean time gap will be <1.5%, meaning the E007 keep was within jitter.

Per-layer profiling will show at least one conv shape running well below the average TFLOP/s. Changing the input padding or crop so the whitening output is 32x32 or 30x30 cuts mean time by >=3%, with accuracy within +-0.15 pp.

A faithful airbench94_muon port without lookahead scores >=0.5 pp lower mean accuracy at 9 epochs than the same Muon setup with lookahead kept, i.e. Muon's update normalization does not replace averaging.

Offline in drafts/, evaluating the tip on extra seeds (3-10) gives a per-seed sd of 0.15-0.3 pp, and an extra-seed mean within 0.15 pp of the seeds 0-2 mean. So the 3-seed gate neither flatters nor penalizes the tip.

Cheap vectorized GPU augmentation that adds diversity without adding difficulty (random brightness/contrast) raises accuracy per epoch at 9 epochs. Heavier augmentation (cutout 12, translate 4) is tuned for 37 epochs and would hurt here.
Adding mild random brightness/contrast jitter on the GPU to the tip at 9 epochs gives >=+0.2 pp mean accuracy at <=1% more time.

structured_output.summary:
I brought the tree in line with E000–E010. Several nodes are now closed:
- **Supported:** H1.1 and H1.1.1 (the base recipe clears the bar at 9–10 epochs). H1.1.2 is supported after being rewritten as "the knee is in (8.5, 9] epochs"; its original "at least 1 extra epoch needed" clause is refuted.
- **Refuted:** H1.1.3 (the slope is not linear and is below 0.4 pp per epoch), H1.3 and H1.3.1 (label smoothing 0.2 and 0.3 give the same result), H2.2 and H2.2.1 (the train step is GPU-bound, not launch-bound; I took E010 off H2.2 because it was misattributed there), and H3 (fixed overhead is about 2%, not over 10%). H3.1 and H3.2 stay supported as maintenance items.
- **Retired:** H2.1 and H2.1.1, because compile, channels_last and bf16 have been in the base since E001 and E007 tested something else.
- **Supported:** H4.2 and H4.2.1 (lookahead is worth about 1 pp; I dropped the clause claiming it reduces spread).

H4.1 now holds an explicit noise model and is marked inconclusive. Bit-identical reruns are deterministic, but any code change re-draws the 3-seed mean with an sd of about 0.09 pp, and time jitter is about 1%.

Several nodes were restated:
- **H1:** the new target is a knee below 8 epochs, at 7.3 s or less.
- **H2:** headroom is now about 5–10% from cutting work, with lower confidence.
- **H4:** the binding constraint is the local 0.753 gate, with winner's-curse risk.
- **H1.2.1:** Muon with lookahead kept and batch size 1024, compared at 9 epochs.
- **H1.4.1:** a self-scoring version with no separate proxy model, at low priority.
- **H1.5.1:** widening beyond the current 576 channels.

New nodes:
- **N1 (end-of-training noise, the top lever):** averaging and lr-tail changes, plus a combined 8.5-epoch target.
- **N2:** an lr/wd/momentum sweep.
- **N3:** an 8.75-epoch test of the knee.
- **N4 (non-conv kernels):** E010 is its first evidence, and N4a tests SiLU or ReLU in place of GELU.
- **N5 (conv-shape inefficiency):** a cold-cache paired rerun that checks whether the E007 keep was noise, and a test of the whitening output shape.
- **N6:** whether Muon needs lookahead.
- **N7:** checking the tip on extra seeds.
- **N8:** mild brightness/contrast augmentation.

Suggested priority: N1a/N1b, then N3, then H1.2.1 and N6, then N4a, then N2a, then H1.5.1.
